messages:
kevin: Heads-up: after the FP8 rollout we see a regression on a couple customer workloads. p50 latency +12%, tokens/s -9% under continuous batching. Suspect batch-shape switching triggers slower kernel choices + KV warmups. Repro below.
maria: Can you paste the profiler traces? image or flame would help.
kevin: attaching minimal trace excerpt: 
```
selector: consider_kernels: [int8_gemm(shape=64x1024,cost=0.92ms), fp8_gemm(shape=128x1024,cost=1.75ms)]
chosen: fp8_gemm(shape=128x1024)  // because estimated mem-copy overhead lower with current model
batch_shapes: [ (len=32,seq=128)->shape128, (len=4,seq=64)->shape64 ]
KV-cache-misses: +23% during shape switch
```
kevin: note: when shapes mix we see the batcher switch to the larger fp8 kernel which has higher per-op latency here (contrary to expectations) — seems cost model underestimates padding waste.
sanjay: I think two factors: 1) cost model ignores padding bytes -> switching favors wider kernels. 2) FP8 calibration path currently performs per-layer fallback for a few ops when calibration error > thresh, and that triggers extra mem copies (device->host->device in our trace) which kills throughput.
val: Interesting: KV cache alignment might matter. When batch shapes change, kv-cache concatenation code realigns bundles; with quantized tensors the stride changes and we hit an expensive path that does memcpy+repack. I saw this on the bench: memcpy spikes align with kernel-switch events.
amy: Quick experiment proposal: 1) make batcher prefer kernel-stability over nominal cost for small delta (i.e., avoid switching unless cost_delta > 15%). 2) include padding_bytes * bandwidth in cost model. 3) run a calibration-ablation: force FP8 calibration to use global static scale (no per-layer fallback) to see impact.
kevin: repro command (local perf test):
```
export REDWOOD_BATCHER_MODE=continuous
export REDWOOD_BATCHER_PACK_THRESHOLD=0.12  # lower => prefer stability
export REDWOOD_QUANT_POLICY=fp8_dynamic
wrk -c 64 -t 8 -d 120s http://localhost:8080/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer ..." -s scripts/mix_shapes.lua
```
kevin: Observed timeline (snippet): 
12:01:03 - start load
12:01:18 - p50 jump +12% coincides with kernel switch log
12:01:19 - KV repack memcpy 0.9ms spike x 40
12:01:20 - calibration fallback applied on layer 6 -> extra memcpy

sanjay: I'll run the two AB tests: (A) pin int8 kernel for shapes <=64, (B) enhanced cost model including padding_bytes*bandwidth. I'll run on the perf-cluster and tag results.
val: Add a metric: "kernel_switch_count" and "kv_repack_count" to tracing so we can correlate across customers.
amy: If AB shows pinning helps, we can ship a short-term heuristic to avoid switching on mixed shapes while we fix calibration path. Also want to measure quality delta from disabling per-layer fallback.
perf-bot: Scheduled benchmark job #4356 on perf-cluster (tags: fp8-mix-shapes). ETA 45m.
kevin: Assigning @sanjay to run ABs and @val to add tracing. I'll follow up with the perf logs and a short PR for cost-model tweak. :thumbsup:
